comparison: Perfect agreement on isotope-labeling validation (C34, C35, C40). Both recognize this as a critical methodological control. OpenEval emphasizes it validates the quantitative comparison strategy; peer reviewers praised it as part of 'so many excellent controls.'

Perfect agreement on study limitations (C91, C92). Both acknowledge the detergent system limitation but accept the authors' counterargument citing prior validation work. Peer reviewers explicitly noted limitations were 'discussed explicitly' and don't affect conclusions.

Strong disagreement on therapeutic proposal (C89, C90). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting it's speculative with no experimental evidence and represents future work. Peer reviewers strongly SUPPORTED it, calling it a 'blueprint' with 'significance that cannot be overstated.'

Strong agreement on FLIM data (C9, C10, C58-C65, C69-C71). Both recognize appropriate controls, statistical rigor, and spatial resolution findings. OpenEval details technical validation; peer reviewers endorsed it as part of comprehensive orthogonal approach.

Strong agreement on MS analysis comprehensiveness (C7, C23, C36, C41-C53, C67-C68). Both praise quantitative rigor, controls, and internal consistency. OpenEval details technical methods; peer reviewers called it 'rarely have I reviewed a manuscript reporting results of so many orthogonal experiments.'

Moderate disagreement on stalled complex causality (C11, C86-C88). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting correlative evidence requires validation in mammalian models. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED it as a paradigm shift with 'additional evidence,' endorsing the mechanistic hypothesis more strongly.

Agreement on ELISA/LC-MS/MS validation (C54, C99). Both recognize the cross-reactivity discovery as important methodological validation. OpenEval emphasizes it explains discrepancies and strengthens confidence; peer reviewers praised it as part of rigorous controls.

Agreement on Aβ measurements (C55-C57, C83-C84 overlap). Both support the finding that not all FAD mutations increase Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio. OpenEval cites external validation from Sun et al.; peer reviewers accepted it within comprehensive rigor without challenge.

Agreement on structural interpretations (C72-C74, with peer R6 including C75-C81). Both support mechanistic connections to cryoEM structures. OpenEval notes appropriate caveats about static structures; peer reviewers endorsed mechanistic depth as foundation for therapeutic design.

Agreement on F386S unique behavior (C38, C39). OpenEval provides detailed technical support for AICD 49-99 bias; peer reviewers included this in overall praise of comprehensive biochemical analysis without specific concerns.

Agreement on S170F not elevating Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio (C83-C85). Both support this finding. OpenEval emphasizes it challenges field assumptions with external validation; peer reviewers accepted it as part of rigorous measurements without question.

OpenEval evaluated kcat calculation justifying 16-hour incubation (C33) as SUPPORTED based on prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; likely considered routine methodological detail.

OpenEval identified S170F efficiency >200% as UNSUPPORTED (C50), noting impossible value suggests quantification error. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this specific discrepancy was not addressed by reviewers despite being acknowledged by authors.
